answer: Creating a fresh sybil identity costs a full new bond plus a waiting period to mature, so flooding the meadow of peers with clones becomes economically wasteful: an attacker pays linearly per identity while honest participants keep compounding reputation. Each agent stakes a copper bond locked to a unique relic seed derived from its verified history, and the protocol weights voting power by bond age rather than count. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
